fatal_errors: The response does not identify the target lightweight MgAlTiVFeCo alloy or its SPS treatment at 1000 °C.
Refractory-element HEAs are generally high-density materials, directly conflicting with the lightweight requirement; cited evidence E3 explicitly acknowledges their high density.

The proposed chemical-short-range-order mechanism is not established by the cited evidence and omits the target oxide barrier phases, densification, passive-film formation, and diffusion-controlled oxidation.
No quantitative density, hardness, oxidation, or corrosion predictions are supplied, and the relevant 900 °C air and 3.5 wt% NaCl test conditions are absent.
Claims of improved ductility and thermal conductivity-related behavior are not supported by the provided excerpts; refractory HEAs may instead suffer brittleness and oxidation susceptibility.
explanation: The hypothesis is only broadly related through its discussion of HEAs and elevated-temperature strength. It reconstructs neither the material nor the processing-property relationship in the target, which centers on ball-milled BCC MgAlTiVFeCo consolidated by SPS at 1000 °C. The cited papers support the general strength and thermal stability of some refractory HEAs, but they do not validate the asserted SRO mechanism, improved ductility, or lightweight performance. Several excerpts actually expose adverse boundaries—high density, brittleness, oxidation susceptibility, and processing difficulty—that are not incorporated as conflicting evidence. The proposed experiment is generic and lacks temperature-controlled SPS comparisons, oxidation-rate constants, and electrochemical measurements needed to discriminate the target mechanism.
